proposal.hypothesis: Combining T1’s capped OpenMP team and 256-options-per-worker cutoff with four-option SSE2 arithmetic may reduce arithmetic overhead on large inputs, but scalar logf/expf calls and interaction with threading may limit or erase the benefit. The combined program needs its own measurement.

retained: Retained T1’s inline per-option helper, serial cutoff and static OpenMP path with team size capped by min(threads, n).
Added a compile-guarded four-option SSE2 Black-Scholes kernel using unaligned loads, vector arithmetic and CND polynomial evaluation, while retaining scalar logf and expf calls.
Scheduled complete four-option blocks across the capped OpenMP team, handled the final one to three outputs scalarly, and retained scalar parallel fallback for unsupported targets.
